scope: Initial forced skills/list RPC and host/local filesystem implementation; source audit during frozen app build. No auth/config file contents inspected. Caller supplies the default environment filesystem, so custom/remote ExecutorFileSystem implementations can have different I/O boundaries.

pointers.symbol: ConfigBuilder::build; boxed future is not worker handoff

findings.mechanics: Background TUI task issues request_typed SkillsList(force_reload=true). App-server schedules the request separately under shared config serialization. Force clears plugin and skill caches synchronously before awaiting per-CWD reload. Each CWD awaits config, plugins, then skills; result conversion and final ordering are synchronous.
findings.limits: Shared serialization can wait behind an exclusive config writer. This audit does not measure such a wait.

findings.mechanics: When bundled skills are enabled, snapshot resolution calls synchronous install_system_skills before async root resolution. Warm verification still builds and sorts embedded fingerprint items, hashes embedded file contents, and uses std filesystem marker checks. Marker mismatch performs synchronous filesystem rewrite.
findings.limits: Not measured; no assertion this is dominant. The embedded fingerprint is not memoized in this function.

findings.mechanics: Cold plugin loads are guarded by one async semaphore and process configured plugins sequentially. Version directory enumeration/sort, root checks, manifest discovery/read, SHA digest and JSON validation, and legacy hook reads/parsing have no spawn_blocking boundary in this path. Cacheable manifest parsing <=64KiB is serialized under a std Mutex; larger inputs parse outside that cache lock. Plugin skills use the host root loader; MCP/apps combine async I/O with inline parsing.
findings.limits: Plugin install/uninstall/materialization have separate spawn_blocking calls but do not wrap this forced read path. Remote installed plugins are taken from a snapshot here; no claim that this method itself performs a remote catalog fetch.

findings.mechanics: Root and per-file fanout await I/O; frontmatter/metadata parsing, namespace qualification, deduplication, disabled-path resolution, catalog sorting, and response metadata cloning execute synchronously inside async request polls. Cache removal/eviction can also drop existing metadata inline.
findings.limits: buffered/join concurrency does not preempt ready synchronous work. File counts and durations were not sampled.

findings.mechanics: Directory walk runs sync_walk in spawn_blocking. Skill text read runs bounded, cancellation-aware synchronous I/O in spawn_blocking. TRUEOS cap is eight blocking workers; excess work queues. Native Tokio assigns pool-thread admission metadata to both scheduler cores and blocking jobs.
findings.limits: These are the host/local filesystem boundaries; the request can supply a different ExecutorFileSystem. This is an existing task/thread boundary, not proof of independent physical CPU/carrier isolation, nor evidence that the blocking pool is exhausted.

findings.mechanics: TRUEOS Tokio canonicalize/metadata bypass ordinary-platform asyncify and use native async C ABI operations. AsyncFsOperation::ready checks status; pending calls poll_once, self-wakes, then returns Pending. Typed directory metadata/listing also uses native async VFS. Result decoding/path construction stays inline.
findings.limits: Self-wake can generate scheduling traffic, but this source audit does not quantify it or establish it as a stall cause.

bounds.meaning: These are independent fanout/admission limits, not a count of physical CPU threads.

probe_interpretation.client_refresh_span: tui.startup_skills_refresh wraps only the client request_typed future. Its wall duration includes request/response and server wait; its poll times measure client-side work/scheduling, NOT server handler CPU or blocking closure CPU.
probe_interpretation.foreground_event_span: SkillsListLoaded AppEvent sample measures synchronous TUI application of returned metadata, separately from the server request.
probe_interpretation.server_subspan_requirement: To distinguish server inline work, native-FS wait, and blocking queue/run delay, instrument bounded server-stage futures and/or blocking-job queue/run aggregates. No such additional probes were implemented by this audit.
probe_interpretation.correction: Earlier chat suggestion that the client refresh poll timings directly cover server parsing/fingerprint work was incorrect; this record supersedes it.

follow_up_if_new_live_run_still_lags: First compare client refresh wall, post-handoff AppEvent/server sample identities, and actual draft echo timing; do not infer CPU from RPC wall wait.

For a remaining skills-correlated stall, add bounded server-stage spans around bundled verification, plugin cold load, host root loading, and final merge; include count-only cardinalities if needed, no paths or payloads.

Distinguish inline poll time from blocking queue/start/completion and native-FS progress before choosing CPU offload, fanout limits, or cache changes. Avoid moving the whole async request into spawn_blocking or raising worker counts without attribution.
not_established: No proof skills work caused FrameScheduler starvation
No source algorithm or scheduling change proposed as already validated
